entity.name: Gulf Shores Museum
entity.address_line_1: 244 W 19th Ave, Gulf Shores, AL 36542, USA
entity.editorial_summary: Old-timey house, now a museum with permanent & temporary exhibits on local history, plus events.
entity.description: The Gulf Shores Museum offers free admission to the public and features a variety of exhibits exploring the history and culture of Gulf Shores. The museum showcases permanent exhibits including 'Portrait of a Fishing Village' created by residents of the Lagoon Village detailing families who settled along the north side of Little Lagoon during the 19th Century, 'Drawing a Line in the Sand' commemorating the 50th Anniversary Celebration for the City of Gulf Shores in 2007, and 'Hurricanes - What you Need to Know' where guests can learn about hurricanes, their origins, the devastation they create, and how a community rebuilds following a hurricane. The museum also features rotating exhibits and special exhibits that can range from human interest stories to exhibits on loan from various institutions. Programs and events occur throughout the year and vary depending on holiday, event, or demand from the audience.

Beach Safety

The City of Gulf Shores provides seasonal lifeguard services between March and October and encourages the public to swim at the protected public swimming areas (Gulf Place, West 6th Street, and Lagoon Pass) when lifeguards are present. Six full-time beach safety supervisors and seasonal lifeguards make up the City of Gulf Shores Beach Patrol.

Beach Warning Flags 

Before heading out to the beach, check for current beach conditions to ensure you have a safe and fun experience. Beach flags are posted at all public beach areas and lifeguard towers in Gulf Shores. Please remember that the absence of beach flags does not constitute safe swimming conditions. 

Please note: Within the corporate limits of Gulf Shores, it is ILLEGAL to enter the Gulf of Mexico when double red flags are flying. Those who enter the Gulf waters when double red flags are displayed will be subject to a fine and possible arrest

Know before you go!

Checking beach conditions is easy! Before entering the water, please check current conditions in one of the following ways:

Call 251-968-SURF (7873). 
Visit www.gulfshoresAL.gov.
Text "ALBEACHES" to 888-777 to receive daily beach conditions via text message.
Beware of Rip Currents

Rip currents are strong currents of water that quickly flow away from shore at surf beaches. They typically form at breaks in sandbars and near structures such as jetties and piers. Watch the video below for more information on how to identify and escape rip currents.

Click here

 to view the latest rip current & surf report. 

Red Tide

Red tide results from a massive build-up of certain species of microscopic sea organisms known as dinoflagellates. These organisms produce a toxin that affects the central nervous system of fish so they are paralyzed and cannot breathe. At high concentrations, the organisms may produce a discoloration of the water. Red tides are often referred to as “blooms.” The species (Karenia brevis), isolated from waters along the Gulf Coast, may produce toxins that also cause skin irritation and respiratory problems in humans.

Health Department officials advise: 

Avoid the area if you are susceptible to respiratory problems such as asthma or emphysema.
Leave the water if you experience skin irritations while swimming or boating and rinse immediately with fresh water.
If you experience nose, throat or eye irritation when exposed to the gulf mist, avoid the mist.
Do not eat fish from the red tide-affected area that are lethargic, swim in circles or appear unhealthy.
For addition information, visit www.alabamapublichealth.gov or contact the Alabama Department of Public Health at 334-206-5300.

Summer Programs




June and July 2026
Wednesdays - 2-4PM




Get ready for an unforgettable summer at the museum! This year’s theme, Unearth a Story, invites visitors ages 9-13 years of age to dig into hands‑on activities, creative workshops, and special programs that bring hidden histories to life. Whether you’re exploring interactive exhibits or joining one of our themed events, every visit offers a new story waiting to be uncovered. 

Sign ups are required. 

For more information contact the museum at 251-968-1473 or cshannon@gulfshoresal.gov




 

Gulf Shores Story Walk

Open 10am - Dusk

Step into a story as you stroll through the beautiful butterfly garden behind the museum. A new book is featured each quarter, offering families a fresh reason to visit, read, and explore together. Follow the Storywalk path, read along page by page, and enjoy fun activities along the way. Bring a picnic, relax in the garden, and make a day of it.

You can check out each featured book from the Gulf Shores Library, making this a wonderful way to encourage both reading and outdoor adventure.

The Storywalk is proudly sponsored by the Gulf Shores Museum and the Gulf Shores Library.

Summer Quarter Feature: That’s What Dinosaurs Do by Jory John This selection ties into the summer reading theme, Unearth a Story, inviting young readers to dig into imagination and discovery.

For more information contact the museum at 251-968-1473.

History
Museum Building

Built prior to World War II, the museum building was once a beach house that belonged to the Valerie Cole family of Mobile, Alabama.  It was originally located on West Beach, and it was donated to the City of Gulf Shores following Hurricane Frederic in 1979.  The building has been in use by the City since 1982, first as the library, then as a youth center.  The site chosen for the building was made possible by a generous land donation by Claude O’Connor, and Wade & Pat Ward.  To top it all off, Oyster Bay Baptist Church donated their steeple in 1999 to watch over the garden.

Historic Building Donations

The steeple was built in 1953 by Jack Gates and John Quates, and it housed the very necessary attic fan for the church. A 40-foot mast donated by Walter Nelson and Jimmy Nelson of Nelson’s Boat Yard is used as a flag display. This mast built in 1940, served proudly on the Sea Biscuit Shrimp Boat, who’s first owner was John Calloway. It was made from one giant southern pine harvested in Louisiana. “The Sea Biscuit won first place for decorated boats, in its category, at the very first Shrimp Festival in 1971”, says Walter Nelson. These wonderful donations are only a part of the rich nature history of the Gulf Shores community.

Annexation

Any owner of a property that is contiguous to the current boundary of the City of Gulf Shores may apply for annexation to become part of the City of Gulf Shores.

What is Annexation?

Annexation is the process by which cities extend their municipal services, regulations, voting privileges, and taxing authority to new territories. The result is a change in the boundaries of the community.

Who is Eligible?

Any owner of a property that is contiguous (touching) the current boundary of the City of Gulf Shores may apply for annexation. 

To see if your property is contiguous to the current boundary of the City of Gulf Shores, please click here 
Annexation
to view the Gulf Shores City Limits Map.

What are the Benefits of Annexation? 

The City of Gulf Shores provides several services and protections for the benefit of its citizens. Click here to see the complete list of annexation benefits.

How to Apply for Annexation
Print and fill out the Annexation Application.
Make sure all materials from the checklist in the lower section of the Annexation Application are in order.
Submit completed Annexation Application with all checklist materials to:
City of Gulf Shores Planning and Zoning Department
205 Clubhouse Drive Suite B
P.O. Box 299
Gulf Shores, AL 36542
Once we have received your application, please allow for a twenty day review process that concludes with a City Council hearing which you are recommended to attend.
Fees

There is no fee to apply for annexation.

How can I get married on the beach?

As a rule, weddings are not allowed on the Gulf Shores public beaches. If you are renting a private beach house or condominium, and have the permission of the owners to conduct a wedding, no permits are required from the City. You do need to make your guests aware, however, that they cannot park on the road rights-of-way. No chairs, gazebos, arches, etc. are allowed to be placed on the public beaches. Gulf State Park, located in Gulf Shores, has a pavilion that is perfect for family and group outings, reunions, beach parties and sunset weddings. Rental is available 7 days a week, except major holiday weekends during the summer. For more information on pavilion rentals or to having a wedding on Gulf State Park beaches (permit required), call 251-968-7296 or 968-7245 Wednesday - Sunday. Contact the City Clerk's office at 251-968-1124 for more information from the City of Gulf Shores.

Building Department

Welcome to the City of Gulf Shores Building Department. Our mission is to protect the health, safety, and welfare of our community by ensuring that construction and development within the city meet all applicable building codes, Federal and State regulations and safety standards. We work closely with homeowners, contractors, developers, design professionals, NFIP and ADEM to support responsible growth while preserving the unique character of Gulf Shores.

The Building Department provides a full range of services including plan review, permitting, inspections, code enforcement, coastal resource preservation, and flood regulation compliance. Whether you are planning a new project, renovation or routine maintenance, our knowledgeable staff are here to guide you through process efficiently and professionally. We are committed to delivering clear guidance, timely service, and consistent enforcement to help your project move with confidence.

Business License and Tax Requirements

Thank you for your interest in doing business in our beautiful city. We wish you well as you pursue your desires toward a successful and prosperous business.

A valid City of Gulf Shores business license is required for any company or person engaged in business within the corporate limits as well as our police jurisdiction. A business license application needs to be completed and submitted for approval as well as the fee(s) paid before conducting business in the city.

There are 2 different types of license applications: a general business license and a rental license application. If you are operating your business from more than one location or have more than one rental property a separate application and license will be required for each location. Along with the business license requirements there may be taxes associated with your type of business. Below you will find more information and links to our business license applications, checklists and tax forms. Please review the required information before submitting a business license application.

Applying to the City of Gulf Shores

Employment applications will be accepted only when job openings occur.  To apply for an open position, you must apply online through our career portal or complete an  application form and submit to Human Resources via email at hr@gulfshoresal.gov, or deliver by mail to:

City of Gulf Shores Human Resources
P.O. Box 299
Gulf Shores, AL 36547
(251) 968-2425

The City of Gulf Shores is a Drug-Free Workplace and an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Current Employment Opportunities 

Current Employment Opportunities with the City of Gulf Shores are listed online via our Career Portal on GovernmentJobs.com. If you do not see any listings on our listing page, there are currently no open positions.

Applications are accepted for open positions only.
